english.title: Obstruct officer - power of entry - terrorism
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wilfully obstructed an authorised officer of the Secretary of State acting in the exercise of a power conferred by a warrant under section 52 of the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001
english.legislation: Contrary to section 52(6)(a) and (7) of the Anti-Terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A constable who enters premises under the authority of a warrant may give such assistance as an authorised officer may request for the purpose of facilitating the exercise of any power under this section; and search or cause to be searched any person on the premises who the constable has reasonable cause to believe may have in his possession any document or other thing which may be required as evidence for the purposes of proceedings in respect of an offence under section 47 (nuclear weapons) or section 50 (offences outside the UK). (section 52(3).
(ii) The warrant may be executed at any time within one month from the time of the issue.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
